title: Preservation outside a disjoint segment
statement: Let $\mu,\mu':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,b,n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $l$ be a finite list of natural numbers. Suppose that at every index $b+i$ for $i<|l|$, the function $\mu$ equals the integer represented by $l_i$. Suppose also that $\mu'(j)=\mu(j)$ whenever $j<a$ or $a+n\le j$, and that either $b+|l|\le a$ or $a+n\le b$. Then at every index $b+i$ for $i<|l|$, the function $\mu'$ equals the integer represented by $l_i$.
hypotheses_covered: A list l of natural numbers
The function μ agrees with the integer cast of l at every index in the segment starting at b
The functions μ and μ' agree at every index j with j < a or a + n ≤ j
The segment and interval are separated: b + |l| ≤ a or a + n ≤ b
